clue.text: Spinner using heavy atmosphere against one in the middle

indicators.note: in tells us one pair of pieces is set inside the word for the middle

parts.note: the middle is the centre

indicators.note: against means placed right up beside, so the two short pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a fug is a stuffy, heavy atmosphere in a room

explanation.surface: A spinning machine works by pushing thick air against something at its core.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' sets the two short pieces side by side, and 'in' places them within the word for the middle; the spinner is a laboratory machine, not a top or bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: A centrifuge is a machine that spins samples at high speed, so it is literally a spinner.

clue.text: Party posturing

explanation.surface: Theatrical showing off at a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A camp is a faction or party in a dispute, and camp also means affected or theatrical posturing.

clue.text: No end of humiliation for a boy who is unimportant?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the following word

parts.note: per means for each, for a
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A lad is spared the last of his shame, as he is a nobody anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonperson is someone treated as having no significance, an unimportant individual.

clue.text: Unprecedented release just becoming known

parts.note: a record is a recording released to the public
breaking news is news just coming out

explanation.surface: A ground-breaking album is being launched as we speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A record-breaking feat beats all previous ones, so it has no precedent.

clue.text: Female commander, no longer fresh, concentrated

parts.note: OC is Officer Commanding
used goods are no longer fresh or new

explanation.surface: A woman officer, past her prime, kept her mind on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Focused attention is concentrated attention, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Faux pas about leaders of Irish Republic, one reaching highest places

indicators.note: about means around, so the blunder wraps the other letters

parts.note: a gaffe is a faux pas

indicators.note: leaders of picks the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: An embarrassing blunder involving Irish political chiefs, one of whom rose to the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the blunder round the leaders' initials; the definition playfully describes a tall animal browsing treetops.
explanation.definitionFit: The giraffe, tallest of animals, reaches leaves in the highest branches.

clue.text: As Prince, I travel with King

parts.note: to travel is to go
R (Rex) is the abbreviation for King

explanation.surface: Someone playing a prince journeys about with the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Igor is the title hero of Borodin's opera; 'As' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Igor is the name of the Russian prince in Borodin's opera, so a prince by that name.

clue.text: Group of craftsmen producing coin once without Queen's inscription

indicators.note: without means the named letters are taken away

parts.note: the guilder was the Dutch currency before the euro
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is inscribed on British coins and post boxes

explanation.surface: Artisans made a former coin that lacks the royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: A guild is a medieval association of craftsmen or merchants.

clue.text: Tipped with regenerated limbs?

explanation.surface: Given a gratuity, plus new arms and legs.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'remember' a waiter is to tip them; read as RE-MEMBERED it means given members again.
explanation.definitionFit: Remembering a servant means giving a tip, and re-membered playfully means having limbs restored.

clue.text: Old-fashioned, like our competitors slow on to a story?

definitions.text: like our competitors slow on to a story?

explanation.surface: Rival papers are dated and late on the news.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue appeared in The Times, so 'our competitors' are other newspapers trailing The Times on a scoop.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind the times means outdated, and literally describes papers lagging this newspaper.

clue.text: Insane fellow from Scotland touring another part of the UK

indicators.note: touring means going around, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: Mac is a common term for a Scotsman
NI is Northern Ireland, part of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A mad Scot goes on a trip round a different corner of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Manic describes wild, frenzied behaviour, a near synonym of insane in loose use.

clue.text: Vehicle allowance has run out, so make the most of today

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: out says the letter for run is removed from the combined pieces

parts.note: a per diem is a daily expenses allowance
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: My car expenses have been used up, so I'd better seize the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link; 'out' removes R from CARPERDIEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpe diem is the Latin motto 'seize the day', an exhortation to make the most of the present.

clue.text: Hard things to hear from Solomon?

definitions.text: Hard things to hear from Solomon?

parts.words: Hard things to hear from Solomon?
parts.note: pearls are hard gems, and the biblical King Solomon was famed for wise sayings, so his sayings are precious hard things you might hear

explanation.surface: Unwelcome remarks one might get from a famously wise king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard things to hear' suggests unwelcome news; really it means hard objects (pearls) that are heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Wise sayings are known idiomatically as precious gems of advice, and Solomon is the byword for wisdom.

clue.text: Going to the match, one may be at the back of the train

definitions.text: Going to the match, one may be at the back of the train

parts.words: Going to the match, one may be at the back of the train
parts.note: the match is a wedding, not a football game, and the train is the bride's gown trailing behind

explanation.surface: A fan heading to a game stands at the rear of the railway carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' and 'train' suggest sport and rail travel; they are a marriage and a wedding dress train.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridesmaid attends the bride at a wedding and often carries her train.

clue.text: Pretty young woman's bloomer, when tight

explanation.surface: A lovely girl's underwear is far too snug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests underwear; it is a flower, and a tight one is still in bud.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosebud is an old term for a pretty young girl, and literally a rose flower not yet opened.

clue.text: Champion's mount cheated of first at winning post

parts.note: the winning post marks the end of a race

indicators.note: cheated of first means robbed of its opening letter

parts.note: a horse is a rider's mount

explanation.surface: A title-winner's horse was robbed of victory right at the finishing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 's' stands for 'is' and 'at' is a link; ORSE (HORSE less its first letter) follows END.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause is to support it, which is what endorsing it means.

clue.text: Back in power? Let decree 'get worked out

indicators.note: worked out suggests solved or reshaped, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: Allow the official order to be sorted out.
explanation.definitionFit: A politician re-elected is voted in again, so returned to power.

clue.text: Son in study group is extremely thick

parts.note: a den is a private study

indicators.note: in means the letter for son is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: A boy in the study circle is very dim indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: Densest is the superlative of dense, so most thick, whether in substance or in wit.

clue.text: English author? Wrong an American one

indicators.note: wrong means not right, so these letters are set out incorrectly in a new order

explanation.surface: Was this writer English? No, he was a Yankee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English author?' looks like a question; it is fodder, E plus AUTHOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry David Thoreau, who wrote Walden, was an American author.

clue.text: Manage to get a herb containing drug

indicators.note: containing means the herb wraps around the drug letter

parts.note: chive is a herb
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Arrange to obtain a herb laced with narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve something is to manage to bring it about, a close synonym.

clue.text: Holy person has job drinking beer? On the contrary!

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so one piece goes inside another
on the contrary swaps the roles, so the beer takes in the job instead

parts.note: ale is beer
a post is a job

explanation.surface: A saint with a job that involves drinking beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, the job drinks the beer; 'On the contrary!' swaps the roles, so the beer holds the job.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is one of Christ's disciples, a holy person.

clue.text: Note stone crumbling at back of store in Northern town

indicators.note: at back of means the scrambled letters follow the word for store

parts.note: stock is a store of goods

indicators.note: crumbling stone falls apart, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A note about decaying masonry behind a shop in a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbling' rearranges NOTE STONE into TONONTEES, placed 'at back of' STOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockton-on-Tees is a market town in north-east England, on the River Tees.

clue.text: Suspended? Previously one would be kept in

indicators.note: kept in means held inside the other word

parts.note: once means formerly, previously
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Was it suspended? Before, someone would have been held back.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans put on ice are suspended or postponed, an idiom from keeping things chilled.

clue.text: Drop bit off necklace, say

explanation.surface: A part has fallen from a string of jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: A bead is a small drop of liquid, and also one of the pieces threaded on a necklace.

clue.text: Dressing improves this food, gutting good nitrogen into it

indicators.note: into it says the new letters go inside the word for food

parts.note: aliment is a formal word for food or nourishment
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A salad dressing would improve this dish, with extra goodness and fertiliser put in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutting' is best read as a misprint for 'putting', a link with 'into it'; dressing is lining soldiers up in ranks, not salad dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressing ranks in drill means lining soldiers up straight, which improves their alignment.

clue.text: Fancy woman losing three sons in joint!

indicators.note: losing means the letters for the sons are taken away

parts.note: a fancy woman is a mistress
S is the abbreviation for son, so three sons give three S

explanation.surface: A kept woman parts from her three boys and ends up in a smoky bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The three S letters are scattered through MISTRESS; all go, leaving the carpentry joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitre is a woodworking joint made by cutting two pieces at an angle.

clue.text: Food and drink in parliament

explanation.surface: Meals and wine are served in the legislature.
explanation.definitionFit: Diet means what one eats and drinks, and also a legislative assembly as in Japan's Diet.

clue.text: Police officers two similar men replaced

parts.note: supers are police superintendents

indicators.note: two similar means the same short piece appears twice

parts.note: Ed is a man's name, standing for a man here

explanation.surface: Senior detectives were swapped for a pair of lookalike blokes.
explanation.definitionFit: To supersede is to take the place of something, so superseded means replaced.
